rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 (score 39.81) is the best-tested design. It differs from iteration 1 (33.89) only in ki, 0.1 to 0.5, and that change raised the oval progress and score. Every design so far has left the line on every track, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.066 and 1 to 2 line-loss events. Iteration 4 (26.98) widened the sensors and scored lower, so sensor span is not the lever. Iteration 2 (26.36) changed wheel_track to 0.14 along with kp, kd, ki and speed, so it cannot isolate the wheel track effect.

What I kept from the critiques: the iteration-3 geometry (5 sensors at x ±0.032 and ±0.016, y 0.05, size 0.012, wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8) and the iteration-3 controller (kp 3.0, kd 0.03, base_speed 1.5, last_direction). The critiques agree that the iteration-3 baseline is the right comparison point.

What I changed: ki 0.5 to 0.8, a single variable. The earlier step from 0.1 to 0.5 helped, so a further moderate step tests whether more integral action keeps reducing the departure. The integral cap of ±2 gives at most 1.6 turn units, which is bounded and avoids the 3-unit maximum of ki 1.5 that the critique called an untested overclaim.

What I rejected: the draft's ki 1.5 (too large a jump, and its rationale did not match its controller values); its kp 1.5, base_speed 1.0 and kd 0.1 (untested in combination, and kd 0.1 gives edge kicks larger than kp); its wheel_track 0.14 (the iteration-2 result is confounded, and the 39.8 baseline uses 0.12); and its sensor changes. I did not change the start behaviour, since no tool here alters initial alignment.

Expected result (hypothesis): a score at or above 39.8, with oval progress at or above 0.1675 and line-loss events at or below 2 per run. If max_error falls below 0.06 or line-loss events drop, bias removal is helping and ki can rise further next round. If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.066 with the same early timing, the cause is the start or first bend, and the next change must target that. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 or the score falls below 39.8, revert to ki 0.5.
